findings.title: Cycle intersection in Theorem 15.3.1
findings.summary: The proof establishes representation independence for delta-preforms using the assumed cycle-intersection theorem. Its associativity and commutativity use the corresponding properties of the cycle product.

findings.title: The Fulton–Sturmfels input in Theorem 15.6.1
findings.evidence: the identification and the diagonal-degeneration formula are used here as inputs
findings.summary: The chapter uses the identification of operational Chow cohomology with Minkowski weights and the fan-displacement product as an input. The subsequent argument invokes their compatibility under refinement.

findings.title: Fan refinement in Proposition 15.6.2
findings.evidence: Assume the toric fan product and its refinement compatibility.
findings.summary: The pointwise tangent-fan calculation transfers the construction to smooth polyhedral weights under the toric product and refinement assumptions.

findings.title: Comparing the polyhedral products of GK and CLD25
findings.evidence: An identification on a chosen class still requires matching the calibration, the allowable generators, and the current realization.
findings.summary: A comparison on a specified common class requires matching the calibrations, permitted generators and realization as currents. The chapter discusses this as a comparison requirement.

findings.title: Geometric inputs to the algebra of delta-forms
findings.evidence: pullback and intersection of ambient tropical preforms must already be constructed
findings.summary: The algebraic argument assumes the geometric constructions for ambient tropical preforms, including their projection and closedness properties. It does not prove those constructions.

findings.title: Geometric detection in Proposition 16.4.1
findings.evidence: The nondegeneracy of local wedge detection, proved for the analytic presentation spaces in the cited comparison, forces the original form to vanish.
findings.summary: The reduction to top degree uses the vanishing criterion and nondegeneracy of local wedge detection in the cited analytic presentation spaces. The comparison uses these geometric inputs in addition to the dimension argument.

findings.title: A proper pushforward on currents needs a delta-form presentation
findings.summary: Properness gives a candidate pushforward on currents by transposition. Preservation of delta-forms requires additional control of local ambient presentations. A balanced polyhedral pushforward alone can fail this requirement.

findings.title: Embedding original Gubler–Künnemann delta-forms into Mihatsch’s sheaf
findings.evidence: the source states this comparison without a formal proof
findings.summary: The stated comparison is in the common algebraic category. A proof is needed that the formula on ambient generators descends to the original Gubler–Künnemann sheaf and gives an embedding.

findings.title: Surjectivity of weak-current restriction in Proposition 17.2.11
findings.evidence: the original CLD test-space topology is the induced subspace topology
findings.summary: Hahn–Banach gives surjectivity under the induced-topology premise from GJR. That premise is an input to the argument.

findings.title: Density of original smooth tests in the weak test topology
findings.evidence: Density is a separate question; it does not follow from the inclusion of sheaves.
findings.summary: The manuscript leaves density as a separate question for uniqueness of extension. The Hahn–Banach extension supplies a continuous functional under the stated topology premise. Positivity of the extension also requires its own argument.

findings.title: Canonical metrics in the original Gubler–Künnemann theory
findings.summary: The original argument used smoothness of the canonical tropicalization. The corrected harmonicity statement leaves open whether these canonical metrics admit a presentation in the original delta-metric theory. The later discussion in this chapter concerns the same gap.

findings.title: Comparison of the CLD25 and GJR harmonic sheaves
findings.evidence: requires a PL curvature comparison with matching hypotheses, and then a comparison of their chart presentations
findings.summary: Matching the sheaves requires comparing numerical triviality with vanishing of the original curvature current in matching PL classes, then comparing the resulting chart presentations. The cited degree-one result treats the numerical/current step for its integral PL metrics.

findings.title: Comparing currents across actual test spaces
findings.evidence: One needs density for uniqueness and a continuity estimate for existence.
findings.summary: Proposition 18.6.1 proves an abstract criterion. Its use on actual differential test spaces requires density for uniqueness and a continuous seminorm bound for extension. Preservation of positivity, closedness, products and geometric presentations requires further hypotheses.

findings.title: Continuous mixed currents in the comparison chain
findings.evidence: the continuous product theorem defines local mixed currents
findings.summary: This step uses the mixed-current construction and stability for the prescribed local approximation class. The existence and independence discussed in Theorem 11.1.5 and the multiplier convergence in Proposition 13.1.1 each carry explicit proof obligations.
